chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mithammi, from Is'haq ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Imam is ahead of me by one rak'ah, so it happens to be one for me and two for him. So, should I perform the Tashahhud every time I sit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, for rather, the Tashahhud is a Blessing.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: The sitting and recitation of testimony (Tashahhud) in prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةُ: A unit of prayer (bowing and prostration)

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if the Imam is ahead by one rak'ah during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a follower is one rak'ah behind the Imam, they must perform the Tashahhud after every single rak'ah rather than waiting until the end, ensuring their prayer remains connected to the Imam's. This ruling highlights the theological significance of *ittiba'* (following) in congregational prayer, where the Tashahhud is not merely a concluding ritual but a continuous act of blessing (*barakah*) that validates the follower's participation in the Imam's prayer.
